text:
sara: hitting a DSAR delete failure for request DSAR-2026-172 — privacy-proxy returns 403 KMS decrypt failed. :frowning:
axel: can you paste the error/logs?
kevin: flagging — delete path touches KMS decrypt, not just object metadata. if key access is blocked, deletes will fail.
sara: error snippet: 
```
ERROR: DecryptError: crypto key access denied
    at KMSClient.decrypt (/srv/privacy-proxy/src/kms.js:87:15)
    requestId=DSAR-2026-172 userId=acct_993
```
axel: looking at IAM audit, saw a removal of a binding on the eu key around ~4076540000. who made the change?
liz: that was me — I removed a wildcard decrypter binding to tighten cross-tenant scopes. i didn't realize privacy-proxy relied on that SA; my fault. :grimacing:
mira: legal — we need deletion within the statutory timeline. if we can't delete immediately we must document the delay and provide timeline to the requester.
ops-oncall: rolling RBAC forward/back is delicate. propose: add a scoped binding for privacy-proxy SA on the specific CMK, with an audit justification and short TTL, then run the delete retry.
audit-bot: IAM policy change detected: user=liz action=remove role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter resource=projects/redwood-ops/locations/eu-west1/keyRings/embeddings/cryptoKeys/redwood-eu-embeddings
kevin: workaround options: (1) re-grant decrypter to privacy-proxy SA, (2) route delete through a key the admin controls (not available if keys are non-exportable). option 1 is the only feasible immediate path.
sara: DSAR ticket: https://support.redwood.internal/dsar/DSAR-2026-172. user proof verified. can't delay much.
axel: i'll prepare an IAM change: add binding `serviceAccount:privacy-proxy@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com -> roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter` on key redwood-eu-embeddings. will include justification "restore privacy-proxy decrypt for DSAR-2026-172" and set a 1h TTL in the change description.
liz: approved. i'll also open a PR to infra-policy to add an explicit exception list for privacy-proxy keys so this doesn't happen silently again.
mira: legal wants retention-exception record only if deletion is delayed. prefer to avoid exception; please prioritize immediate completion and attach audit proof.
kevin: after RBAC fix we also need to ensure there are no stale snapshots referencing the old key. i'll run `scripts/list-embeddings --owner acct_993` and then `scripts/purge-embedded --owner acct_993 --key=redwood-eu-embeddings`.
ops-oncall: performing IAM change now. will monitor Cloud Audit Logs and KMS access logs, and kick off the retry job. ETA ~12m.
audit-bot: change queued: actor=axel justification="restore privacy-proxy decrypt for DSAR-2026-172" ttl=3600s
axel: pushed change; monitoring logs.
audit-bot: change completed by axel at 4076543245. policy change id=chg-2026-907.
kevin: delete retries started. progress: 73 items queued.
kevin: delete retries succeeded: 73/73 items removed, manifest generated.
mira: legal confirms closure; please attach deletion manifest and KMS access audit snippet for the DSAR record.
sara: attaching manifest: https://redwood.internal/records/DSAR-2026-172/manifest and KMS audit excerpt: https://redwood.internal/audit/kms/DSAR-2026-172
liz: following up with infra-policy PR: add pre-deploy check to block removing roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter from keys that have active privacy-proxy bindings. i'll reference this incident. :thumbsup:
sara: closing thread — filing a short postmortem tag for follow-up and adding remediation checklist to the DSAR runbook. thanks all.
